papers.title: Deciphering conserved and divergent tissue architectures via soDGVAE-mediated spatial transcriptomics integration.
papers.abstract: Spatial omics has revolutionized our understanding of molecular heterogeneity within its native tissue context. However, the integrative analysis of datasets spanning replicate samples, disparate platforms, different developmental stages, and cross-species remains a challenging computational task.
papers.summary: The authors present soDGVAE, a computational method for integrating spatial transcriptomics datasets across replicates, platforms, developmental stages, and species. The approach aims to distinguish conserved versus divergent tissue architectures, addressing a key challenge in comparative spatial omics analysis.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral arter
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing across days 1, 7, and 14 after ischemic stroke with spatial transcriptomics at day 7 to map how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration relates to neuroimmune and neuronal signaling. It identifies cell-type-specific and spatially heterogeneous responses that may shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling, providing a resource for understanding MSC-associated repair mechanisms.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Multi-Omics Reveals Primate-Specific Mechanisms of Liver Regeneration Following Partial Hepatectomy.
papers.abstract: The liver is a vital metabolic organ with an extraordinary capacity for regeneration, making it a key focus for understanding tissue repair and developing therapeutic strategies for liver diseases. However, ethical limitations restrict liver regeneration research largely to rodents, leaving critical gaps in our understanding of primate-specific mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses spatiotemporal multi-omics to profile liver regeneration after partial hepatectomy in a primate model, addressing the gap left by rodent-only studies. It identifies primate-specific molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying liver regeneration, which may inform therapeutic strategies for human liver disease.

papers.title: CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis.
papers.abstract: The updated CellMarker 3.0 resource (http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CellMarker) offers a comprehensive resource, integrating experimentally validated and robustly algorithm-predicted marker genes for diverse cell types across human and mouse tissues. In addition, web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data are described. CellMarker 3.0 was updated with more data and new features, including (i) appending 274 tissues, 1877 cell types, 64 040 markers, and 1 245 923 tissue-cell type-marker entries over the previous version. The current release con
papers.summary: CellMarker 3.0 is an updated database that combines manually curated, experimentally validated cell marker genes with computationally predicted markers for many cell types across human and mouse tissues. It adds substantial new content (274 tissues, 1,877 cell types, 64,040 markers) and introduces interactive web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data. The resource aims to help researchers identify and annotate cell types in single-cell and spatial studies.

papers.title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
papers.abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing plat
papers.summary: The authors developed droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing methods, dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT, which combine a commercial microfluidic device with nanopore sequencing to profile chromatin accessibility and histone modifications in individual cells at high throughput. This addresses the previous scalability limitations of long-read single-cell epigenomics, enabling multidimensional regulatory element profiling within single cells.

papers.title: Cell3D: a comprehensive database for interactive 3D visualization and crosstalk analysis of single-cell and spatial omics.
papers.abstract: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics yield large-scale, high-dimensional datasets. However, cross-feature integrative exploration is constrained, since most current platforms support a single data type and lack interactive visualization for multi-feature analysis. To address this unmet need, we developed Cell3D, an accessible and versatile interactive platform designed to advance integrative multi-level feature analysis. Cell3D curates 898 publicly available datasets, comprising 397 single-cell and 501 spatial transcriptomic datasets, encompassing 2 924 646 single cells and spatial spots ac
papers.summary: Cell3D is a new database and interactive platform that curates 898 public single-cell and spatial transcriptomics datasets (397 single-cell, 501 spatial), covering nearly 3 million cells and spatial spots. It enables 3D visualization and cross-feature crosstalk analysis across multiple data types, addressing the limitation of existing platforms that typically support only one data type and lack interactive multi-feature exploration.

papers.title: Stromal CCL2/CXCL10/SPARC axes drive pro-tumor CHI3L1 expression for microenvironmental modulation in pancreatic cancer progression and therapeutic innovation.
papers.abstract: Chitinase-3-like-protein 1 (CHI3L1), a low-abundance protein in normal tissues, is markedly upregulated in the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), where it promotes fibrosis and immune evasion. Spatial transcriptomics revealed enrichment of CHI3L1 at tumor-stroma interfaces, suggesting that cell-cell interactions regulate CHI3L1 expression.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to show that CHI3L1, a pro-fibrotic and immune-evasive protein, is enriched at tumor-stroma interfaces in pancreatic cancer. The authors identify stromal CCL2, CXCL10, and SPARC as signals that drive CHI3L1 expression, highlighting these axes as potential therapeutic targets for microenvironmental modulation.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies SLCO1B3 as a prognostic marker and functional oncogenic driver in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a leading cause of cancer mortality with limited prognostic biomarkers. Given the role of metabolic reprogramming in tumor progression, this study investigated the clinical relevance and biological function of the lipid metabolism-associated transporter SLCO1B3 in HNSCC.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to show that the lipid metabolism transporter SLCO1B3 is associated with prognosis in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and appears to functionally promote tumor growth. The authors propose SLCO1B3 as both a prognostic biomarker and a potential oncogenic driver in HNSCC.

papers.title: Mid-zone hepatocytes trade proliferation for survival via Atf4-Chop axis in early acute liver injury.
papers.abstract: Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Using a mouse model of acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, we show that hepatocytes undergo transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. Although spatial transcriptomics (ST) alone could not independently confirm zonal proliferative restraint, ST analysis identified a unique mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis. By integrating Cut&Run
papers.summary: Using a mouse model of acetaminophen-induced liver injury, the authors show that hepatocytes in the mid-zone of the liver lobule transiently suppress proliferation before later repair, with spatial transcriptomics revealing a mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis. This suggests mid-zone hepatocytes prioritize survival over division early after injury, consistent with zonal drug metabolism.

papers.title: CCCView: A Knowledge Platform for Integrated Analysis of Spatial Transcriptomic Cell-Cell Communication.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables investigation of cell-cell communication (CCC) while preserving spatial context, yet large-scale resources that organize spatial CCC results across studies and make them readily searchable, visualizable, and comparable remain limited. Here, we present CCCView, a knowledge platform integrating 699 spatial transcriptomics samples and 7,473,444 inferred CCC interactions across 24 tissues, 182 annotated cell types, and 27 biological conditions in human and mouse. CCCView uses a unified cell-type annotation workflow and organizes results from three complementary CCC-
papers.summary: CCCView is a new knowledge platform that aggregates cell-cell communication (CCC) results from 699 spatial transcriptomics samples, covering 7.47 million inferred interactions across 24 tissues, 182 cell types, and 27 biological conditions in human and mouse. It standardizes cell-type annotation and organizes results from three complementary CCC inference approaches, making spatial CCC data searchable, visualizable, and comparable across studies. This addresses the current lack of large-scale, integrated resources for spatial CCC analysis.

papers.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an optimized workflow for cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement, and data analysis of small
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes an optimized workflow for preparing small, structurally complex plant tissues for 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics, covering cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement on capture slides, and downstream data analysis. It addresses practical bottlenecks in preserving, orienting, and positioning delicate plant samples within the limited capture area, making spatial transcriptomics more accessible for plant developmental studies.

papers.title: A Cross-Condition Single-Cell Atlas Defines Skeletal Muscle Adaptation and Its Predictive Limits.
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle adapts to diverse stresses through coordinated changes across myofibres and cellular niches, yet these responses are usually studied separately. We assembled a cross-species discovery atlas of 501,940 cells and nuclei from six public resources, comprising 2863 condition-time-state combinations defined at the declared analysis unit level, and evaluated it with two independent validation datasets. Injury produced the largest observed compositional displacement, followed by mechanical overload, whereas acute human endurance exercise and denervation showed smaller occupancy shifts
papers.summary: This study assembled a large cross-species single-cell atlas of skeletal muscle (501,940 cells/nuclei from six public resources) covering many condition-time-state combinations, and validated it against two independent datasets. Injury caused the largest compositional shifts in cell populations, followed by mechanical overload, while acute endurance exercise and denervation produced smaller changes. The work defines a reference framework for muscle adaptation and probes the limits of predicting responses across conditions.

papers.title: Meta-Analysis of ALS Post-Mortem Cerebral Cortex Transcriptome Studies Identifies Robust Shifts in Gene Expression Despite Significant Between-Study Heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Background: ALS is characterized by motor neuron failure with potential neurocognitive comorbidity. Cortical neurons, and their support cells, exhibit pathologic features, some of which have been identified in post-mortem transcriptome studies of the cortex from ALS patients and control subjects. These studies, however, have utilized varying technologies with few attempts to reconcile findings. Methods: This study used meta-analysis to evaluate differential gene expression (ALS vs. control) from 16 prior transcriptome studies utilizing multiple technologies (microarray, bulk RNA-seq or snRNA-s
papers.summary: This meta-analysis integrated 16 post-mortem cerebral cortex transcriptome studies of ALS patients and controls, spanning microarray, bulk RNA-seq, and snRNA-seq technologies, to identify consistent gene expression changes despite substantial between-study heterogeneity. The authors report robust ALS-associated expression shifts in cortical tissue, highlighting the value of cross-study reconciliation for identifying reproducible disease signatures.

papers.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
papers.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. Existing supervised approaches rely on accurate reference data, which are lacking for many cancer types, whereas unsupervised
papers.summary: CDState is a computational method that deconvolves bulk tumor RNA sequencing data into distinct malignant cell states, addressing intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity without requiring single-cell reference data. Unlike supervised approaches that depend on accurate references often unavailable for many cancer types, CDState uses an unsupervised strategy to resolve heterogeneous cell populations from bulk transcriptomes. This enables scalable, cost-effective characterization of tumor cell-state diversity across large cohorts.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omic Analysis of Paired Primary and Peritoneal Metastatic Tumors Reveals GPAA1 as a Therapeutic Target in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Peritoneal metastasis confers a dismal prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC-PM), with median survival rarely exceeding 20 months. Here we employed multi-omic profiling to identify actionable drivers of CRC-PM. We performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) and label-free quantitative proteomics on 13 and 7 matched primary-peritoneal metastasis pairs, respectively. Public single-cell (GSE183916 and GSE132465) and spatial transcriptomic datasets (GSE225857) were integrated to dissect cellular heterogeneity. TCGA cohorts were used for survival analysis, and functional validation was performed in DLD1 c
papers.summary: This study integrates whole-exome sequencing, proteomics, and public single-cell/spatial transcriptomic data from matched primary and peritoneal metastatic colorectal cancer tumors to identify drivers of metastasis. The authors highlight GPAA1 as a potential therapeutic target, supported by survival analysis in TCGA cohorts and functional validation in cell lines. The work provides a multi-omic resource and candidate target for a poorly prognosed metastatic setting.

papers.title: CQRM: A Composite Quantile Regression Model for Differential Expression Analysis of Non-Coding RNA Count Data.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) play important roles in various biological processes, primarily via regulating gene expression at multiple levels. Nevertheless, compared to protein-coding genes, ncRNAs are relatively understudied. They are characterized by low expression, large variation, and more dynamic expression across different tissues and cell types, which creates unique challenges in differential expression (DE) analysis. Methods: We propose the CQRM, an adaptive multi-quantile testing framework for ncRNA count data that incorporates jittering to accommodate discrete cou
papers.summary: The authors propose CQRM, an adaptive multi-quantile testing framework for differential expression analysis of non-coding RNA count data. It uses jittering to handle the discrete nature of counts and tests across multiple quantiles to better capture the low-expression, high-variability profile typical of ncRNAs. This addresses limitations of standard mean-based DE methods for ncRNA data.

papers.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
papers.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from c
papers.summary: This review synthesizes knowledge of the tenocyte–matrix unit across eight orders of magnitude, linking collagen chemistry, fibril and fascicle mechanics, tissue loading, cellular mechanotransduction, and transcriptional responses into a single causal framework. It argues that these chemical, physical, biological, and mathematical descriptions have developed in separate literatures and proposes five transitions as organizing principles. The work is a conceptual integration rather than new experimental data.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to isolate intact multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) from the spleens of mice chronically infected with Leishmania donovani, overcoming a major technical barrier since these cells are normally hard to recover from tissues. They then profiled the transcriptome of these cells, providing the first gene expression signature for MGCs in visceral leishmaniasis. This work offers a resource for understanding how these heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to build a compact risk score predicting pulmonary metastasis or relapse in osteosarcoma, centering on a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated program. The work links an interferon-related gene signature to reduced immune activity and worse metastatic outcomes, and uses single-cell data to characterize the associated immune microenvironment.

papers.title: Beyond Histocompatibility: Donor Tissue Immune States and Their Role in Heart Transplantation.
papers.abstract: Heart transplantation transfers not only donor alloantigens and functional myocardium but also a pre-existing tissue environment shaped by resident immune, vascular, stromal, and parenchymal populations. This review examines the hypothesis that the biological state of donor tissue influences subsequent recipient immunity and contributes to heterogeneity in allograft outcomes. Donor-resident macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and tissue-resident lymphocytes constitute an immunologically active myocardial niche that encounters ischemia-reperfusion injury and recip
papers.summary: This review argues that donor heart tissue carries its own active immune environment—including resident macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and tissue-resident lymphocytes—that shapes how the recipient's immune system responds after transplantation. The authors propose that this pre-existing donor tissue state, beyond just alloantigen matching, contributes to the variability in transplant outcomes. The review synthesizes how ischemia-reperfusion injury and recipient immune responses interact with this donor-derived niche.

papers.title: Pan-Cancer Analysis Identifies LUC7L2 as a Prognostic Biomarker and Potential Functional Regulator of Prostate Cancer Progression.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cancer imposes a substantial global public health burden, and its initiation and progression involve complex dysregulation of gene expression regulatory networks. Methods: This study systematically evaluated the expression characteristics and prognostic value of LUC7L2 across pan-cancer types, with a particular focus on functional validation in prostate cancer. Using transcriptomic and proteomic data from multiple databases, immunohistochemical staining from the Human Protein Atlas, and single-cell transcriptomic datasets GSE137829 and GSE176031, we analyzed the expressi
papers.summary: This study analyzes LUC7L2 expression across many cancer types and finds it is associated with prognosis, with a particular focus on prostate cancer. Using transcriptomic, proteomic, immunohistochemical, and single-cell data, the authors propose LUC7L2 as a prognostic biomarker and potential functional regulator of prostate cancer progression.

papers.title: Scalable localization of clustering instability for spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Standard spatial transcriptomics workflows rely on clustering methods to define regions of interest for down-stream analyses, such as differential expression and pathway enrichment. Although researchers are presented with a single partition, most clustering methods are stochastic, meaning their output depends on random algorithmic choices, typically controlled by a seed; thus, repeating the analysis changing only the seed can yield a different result. Spatial transcriptomics data may be especially sensitive to algorithmic perturbations due to high dimensionality, sparsity, and mixed expression
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a method to identify where clustering results in spatial transcriptomics are unstable across random seeds, rather than relying on a single partition. Because spatial data are high-dimensional, sparse, and mixed, clustering can vary with algorithmic randomness, so the authors propose a scalable way to localize unstable regions. This helps researchers assess confidence in spatial domain definitions before downstream analyses.

papers.title: Spathology: The Birth of Spatial Pathology as a Discipline.
papers.abstract: Pathology has always been a spatial science: for more than 150 years, diagnosis has rested on reading the architecture of cells and tissues. Three technological streams are now converging on this founding principle. Spatially resolved omics can measure thousands of transcripts and over a hundred proteins in intact, formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue; multiplexed imaging quantifies tissue microenvironments cell by cell; and computational pathology has progressed from slide digitization to foundation models that can predict molecular features from morphology. The clinical evidence fo
papers.summary: This perspective argues that spatial pathology is emerging as a distinct discipline from the convergence of three technologies: spatially resolved omics (measuring thousands of transcripts and over a hundred proteins in intact FFPE tissue), multiplexed imaging that quantifies tissue microenvironments cell by cell, and computational pathology foundation models that predict molecular features from morphology. The authors frame this convergence as a return to pathology's founding principle of reading tissue architecture, now augmented by high-dimensional molecular and computational data.

papers.title: Cell-Cell Communication Patterns in Alzheimer's Disease Differ by Cortical Layer.
papers.abstract: Existing cell-cell communication (CCC) studies of Alzheimer's disease dementia (ADD) using cortical snRNAseq data do not account for the distinct cell-type and gene-expression profiles within cortical layers. Cortical-layer-aware CCC analysis may clarify biological mechanisms associated with ADD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI).
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint argues that existing cell-cell communication analyses of Alzheimer's disease using cortical snRNA-seq data ignore the distinct cellular and transcriptional profiles of individual cortical layers. The authors propose a cortical-layer-aware CCC framework to better resolve mechanisms underlying Alzheimer's disease dementia and mild cognitive impairment.

papers.title: NoiBic: a noise-tolerant biclustering algorithm for high-throughput gene expression data analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic technologies generate large-scale gene expression datasets for functional module discovery. However, technical and biological noise can obscure coherent expression patterns and compromise module detection. Noise-tolerant methods are therefore needed to recover meaningful biclusters.
papers.summary: NoiBic is a new biclustering algorithm designed to tolerate noise when discovering coherent gene-expression modules in high-throughput transcriptomic data. It aims to recover meaningful biclusters that conventional methods may miss due to technical and biological noise. The work addresses a practical bottleneck in functional module discovery from large expression datasets.

papers.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing single-cell expression through the lens of topic modeling.
papers.abstract: Gene-expression programs (GEPs) are the co-regulated gene modules whose coordinated activity encodes biological processes. Recovering them from single-cell RNA-seq is hard because regulation is many-to-many. A cell can run several programs at once, and a gene can take part in several. Methods that resolve programs along a trajectory break this structure by assigning each gene to a single program.
papers.summary: PRISM-GEP introduces a topic-modeling approach to recover gene-expression programs (co-regulated gene modules) from single-cell RNA-seq data without forcing each gene into a single program. This addresses the many-to-many nature of gene regulation, where cells run multiple programs simultaneously and genes participate in several, unlike trajectory-based methods that break this structure. The tool lets researchers view single-cell expression through the lens of overlapping, co-regulated modules.

papers.title: Dermatopathology 2030: Navigating the Digital, Computational and Molecular Convergence for Precision Diagnostics-Originated from a Round Table Discussion at A 66, Basel.
papers.abstract: Background: Traditional dermatopathology relies on analog, qualitative pattern recognition, which encounters critical limitations when facing diagnostic "gray zones" and ambiguous tumor proliferations. Objectives: This paper synthesizes a comprehensive framework integrating Whole Slide Imaging (WSI), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and multi-omics to evaluate how this structural convergence redesigns diagnostic risk and safety ecosystems toward 2030. Methods: We analyze the conceptual shift from individual microscope-based observation to multiple data integration. We integrate recent algorithmic
papers.summary: This perspective piece synthesizes a round-table discussion on how dermatopathology is moving from analog microscope-based diagnosis toward an integrated digital workflow combining whole-slide imaging, artificial intelligence, and multi-omics data. The authors argue that this convergence can help resolve diagnostic gray zones and ambiguous tumor proliferations, and they outline a framework for redesigning diagnostic risk and safety practices toward 2030.

papers.title: Cell-Cell Communication in Embryonic Kidney Development: Insights from Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Embryonic kidney morphogenesis depends on the coordinated communication among ureteric epithelium, nephron progenitors, stroma, endothelium and differentiating nephrons. Classical studies established central roles for glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) signaling through the RET proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase (RET), WNT-family signaling, fibroblast growth factor (FGF), bone morphogenetic protein (BMP), Notch, Hedgehog, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) pathways, but pathway-centered models do not fully explain why simila
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are reshaping our understanding of cell-cell communication during embryonic kidney development. It highlights that classical pathway-centered models (GDNF/RET, WNT, FGF, BMP, Notch, Hedgehog, VEGF, PDGF) are insufficient to explain the complexity of morphogenesis, and that spatially resolved, cell-type-specific signaling maps offer a more complete picture of how ureteric epithelium, nephron progenitors, stroma, endothelium, and differentiating nephrons coordinate their development.

papers.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
papers.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug se
papers.summary: The authors present CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that first deconvolves bulk RNA-seq data into cell-type composition and cell-type-specific expression, then uses this to infer drug sensitivity from bulk transcriptomes. This enables drug response to be resolved at cell-type resolution rather than as a single aggregate signal, improving interpretation of heterogeneous tissue samples.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activi
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from public repositories to identify cell adhesion-related gene signatures associated with cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors used Seurat-based single-cell analysis alongside bulk transcriptomic profiling to characterize how these genes are expressed and regulated across cell populations. The work aims to nominate cell adhesion genes as potential therapeutic targets for reducing inflammatory infiltration and preserving blood-brain barrier integrity after stroke.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing with machine learning to characterize the ovarian cancer microenvironment after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The authors identify chronic inflammation signatures and specific cancer-associated fibroblast subsets that are enriched in residual disease and associated with poor clinical outcomes. These findings suggest that targeting inflammatory and fibroblast-driven programs could improve treatment strategies for ovarian cancer.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a transcriptomic aging clock trained with a novel 'age-shift' learning framework that predicts relative biological age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq and microarray data. Pasta's predictions aligned with senescence and stem-like states, and the clock was used to map chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation. This provides a versatile, platform-independent tool for studying aging biology.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are being applied to cancer epigenetics to study how local tissue context shapes regulatory programs in tumors. It argues that while bulk and single-cell sequencing have transformed tumor biology, they lose spatial information, and integrating spatial methods with epigenetic readouts could reveal how microenvironmental organization and cell-cell communication influence tumor heterogeneity.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: This study develops a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue for immunohistochemistry, enabling simultaneous analysis of multiple pigmented eye tissues in mice. Using this approach, the authors built a unified developmental atlas of pigmented ocular tissues, tracking markers like Rpe65, Rhodopsin, and Dct/Tyrp2 alongside re-analysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data. The work provides a coordinated timeline of how pigmented structures in the eye develop together.

papers.title: Condition-Associated Pattern Extraction and Recovery From Multi-Condition Single-Cell RNA-seq Data With CAPER.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in multi-condition single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis is the disentanglement of true biological signals from unwanted variations in complex experimental designs. Current statistical and machine learning-based methods struggle with this task, often providing only visualizable embeddings, over-correcting and discarding biological signal, or failing to resolve cell-type-specific responses. Here, we present CAPER, a matrix factorization framework that explicitly disentangles shared biological states from condition-specific variations. CAPER directly outputs an
papers.summary: CAPER is a matrix factorization framework for multi-condition scRNA-seq that explicitly separates shared biological states from condition-specific variation, rather than producing only visual embeddings. It directly outputs condition-associated expression patterns and recovers them per cell type, addressing over-correction and loss of biological signal common in existing batch/condition correction tools.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 computational pipelines (combinations of normalization methods and clustering algorithms) across three cancer scRNA-seq datasets totaling over 434,000 cells. The authors introduce a Biological Discordance Score to quantify how marker gene interpretation shifts across pipelines, finding that normalization choice affects biological conclusions more than clustering algorithm choice. The work highlights that computational pipeline decisions can materially change downstream biological interpretation in cancer single-cell studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This paper investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, proposing that gut microbes and their metabolites migrate to intervertebral discs and contribute to disc degeneration, a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify the specific microbial species and molecular mechanisms involved in this cross-kingdom communication, though the abstract does not yet report concrete findings. The work sits at the intersection of microbiome research and musculoskeletal disease, potentially opening new avenues for understanding and treating IVDD.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomic Profiling of FAP-Positive Cells in Gastric Cancer and Association with Immunotherapy Efficacy.
papers.abstract: The spatial heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment in gastric cancer, particularly in the stromal compartment, remains poorly characterized. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-positive cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are known to promote tumor progression, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the spatial transcriptional programs of FAP+ and FAP- stroma and their associations with response to immunotherapy are not fully understood.
papers.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to profile FAP-positive versus FAP-negative stromal cells in gastric cancer, aiming to characterize their distinct transcriptional programs within the tumor microenvironment. The authors link these spatial stromal signatures to immunotherapy response, suggesting that FAP+ cancer-associated fibroblasts may shape immune evasion and treatment resistance. The work provides a spatially resolved view of stromal heterogeneity that could inform biomarkers for immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: Identification of ageing-related genes in prostate cancer with type 2 Diabetes using machine learning: a multi-omics study focusing on SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) demonstrates complex associations with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and ageing, though their interconnected molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify and validate diagnostic biomarkers at the intersection of these pathways to enable early detection and risk stratification in high-risk populations. Bioinformatic analysis was performed on PCa and T2DM transcriptomic data downloaded from the GEO database, followed by differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment. Eight machi
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic datasets for prostate cancer and type 2 diabetes to identify genes at the intersection of ageing, diabetes, and prostate cancer biology. Using differential expression, WGCNA, and multiple machine learning methods, the authors nominate SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4 as candidate diagnostic biomarkers, validated through multi-omics analysis. The work is exploratory and biomarker-focused, with limited experimental validation.

papers.title: Topology-adjusted knockout (TAKO): interpretable in silico single-gene knockout ranking on wild-type single-cell gene regulatory networks.
papers.abstract: Predicting single-gene knockout effects from wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data remains challenging when perturbation experiments are costly and existing approaches require knockout-specific model training. Here we introduce Topology-Adjusted Knockout (TAKO), a computationally efficient WT-only framework for single-gene KO impact ranking on single-cell gene regulatory networks. The method applies a strict cut-in-and-out intervention on network transition dynamics and quantifies impact by contrasting stationary propagation profiles before and after perturbation under the same restart distributi
papers.summary: TAKO is a computationally efficient framework that ranks the impact of single-gene knockouts using only wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data, without requiring knockout-specific model training. It applies a strict cut-in-and-out intervention on single-cell gene regulatory network transition dynamics and quantifies impact by comparing stationary propagation profiles before and after perturbation under the same restart distribution. This enables interpretable in silico knockout ranking when perturbation experiments are costly.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis identifies monocyte/macrophage senescence-associated candidate genes in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by immune dysregulation and vascular remodeling. Cellular senescence modulates immune responses, but its role in PAH, particularly in monocytes/macrophages, remains unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify senescence-associated candidate genes associated with monocytes/macrophages in PAH.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic datasets to identify senescence-associated genes specifically in monocytes/macrophages in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The authors propose candidate genes linking immune cell senescence to PAH vascular remodeling, though the abstract does not report experimental validation. The work is exploratory and hypothesis-generating, highlighting a potential role for monocyte/macrophage senescence in PAH pathogenesis.

papers.title: Ferumoxytol potentiates ferroptotic radiosensitization through NCOA4-associated iron mobilization in brain-metastatic lung cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Brain metastasis remains a major cause of mortality in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer, whereas effective radiosensitization strategies are constrained by heterogeneous tumor responses and the tolerance of normal brain tissue. Ferumoxytol, a clinically used iron oxide nanoparticle formulation, has emerging translational potential as an iron-modulating agent. However, whether Ferumoxytol enhances radiosensitivity in brain-metastatic lung cancer cells and the mechanisms underlying this effect remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether ferumoxytol, an FDA-approved iron oxide nanoparticle, can sensitize brain-metastatic lung cancer cells to radiation. The authors propose that ferumoxytol promotes ferroptosis (iron-dependent cell death) via NCOA4-mediated iron mobilization, potentially offering a translational strategy to improve radiotherapy for brain metastases while sparing normal brain tissue.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis reveals the role of PGRN in modulating fibroblast heterogeneity and enhancing wound healing.
papers.abstract: The wound microenvironment plays a crucial role in the skin wound healing process. Fibroblasts, one of the critical cell types within this microenvironment, exhibit significant heterogeneity that influences healing outcomes. Previous studies have demonstrated that progranulin (PGRN) may reduce fibrogenesis during wound healing. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Thus, this study aims to investigate the specific effects of PGRN on fibroblast heterogeneity of skin wound healing in mice.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA-seq to examine how progranulin (PGRN) affects fibroblast heterogeneity during skin wound healing in mice. The authors find that PGRN modulates distinct fibroblast subpopulations, which may explain its previously observed anti-fibrotic effects and its ability to enhance healing outcomes.

papers.title: GlycoRNA-related cellular program scoring identifies Siglec- and myeloid-associated tumor microenvironments for glycoRNA validation.
papers.abstract: Glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) represent a recently recognized connection between RNA biology and cell-surface glycobiology. However, whether glycoRNA-related processes are relevant to human tumors remains unclear, partly because direct glycoRNA measurements are not yet available across large cancer cohorts. We therefore used transcriptomic data to identify tumor settings in which glycoRNA-related programs may be most suitable for further experimental validation.
papers.summary: The authors developed a transcriptomic scoring approach to infer glycoRNA-related cellular programs across human tumors, since direct glycoRNA measurement is not feasible in large cohorts. They identify Siglec- and myeloid-associated tumor microenvironments as the most promising settings for future experimental glycoRNA validation. This is a hypothesis-generating computational study that prioritizes tumor contexts for follow-up work.

papers.title: Integrated Multiomics and Functional Validation Identify CLSPN as a Central Integrator of Genomic Instability and Immune Remodeling in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by pervasive genomic instability, yet the molecular mechanisms linking replication stress responses to genome alteration and phenotypic evolution remain incompletely understood. Here, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis combined with functional validation to investigate the role of CLSPN, a key adaptor of the ATR-CHK1 pathway, in CRC. Machine learning-based feature selection identified CLSPN as a robust prognostic factor. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses revealed that CLSPN is preferentially enriched in highly proliferative tu
papers.summary: This study integrates multiomics data with functional experiments to show that CLSPN, a key adaptor in the ATR-CHK1 replication stress pathway, acts as a central hub linking genomic instability to immune remodeling in colorectal cancer. Machine learning identified CLSPN as a robust prognostic marker, and single-cell/spatial transcriptomics showed it is enriched in highly proliferative tumor regions. The work positions CLSPN as a potential biomarker and mechanistic node connecting replication stress to the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.title: Development and External Validation of an M2 Macrophage-Related Prognostic Signature in Breast Cancer Using Multi-Omics Data and Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), particularly the M2-like phenotype, are central regulators of breast cancer progression; however, clinically applicable models capturing their functional heterogeneity and biological mechanisms remain limited.
papers.summary: This study develops and externally validates a prognostic signature for breast cancer based on M2 macrophage-related genes, using multi-omics data and machine learning. The model aims to capture the functional heterogeneity of tumor-associated macrophages and improve risk stratification. External validation supports its potential clinical utility.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Rora-Associated Aberrant Granulosa Cell Differentiation in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by follicular developmental arrest, yet the molecular basis underlying impaired granulosa cell (GC) differentiation remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics to profile granulosa cells in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), revealing aberrant differentiation states associated with the transcription factor Rora. The findings suggest that disrupted Rora-related regulatory programs contribute to the follicular developmental arrest characteristic of PCOS.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics combined with machine learning to unravel the heterogeneity of cholangiocarcinoma and the WFDC3-mediated prognostic regulatory mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) exhibits substantial cellular heterogeneity and a complex tumor microenvironment (TME), contributing to poor clinical outcomes. Effective prognostic biomarkers and a deeper understanding of the cellular ecosystems associated with high-risk disease remain urgently needed.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial multi-omics data with machine learning to characterize cellular heterogeneity and the tumor microenvironment in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The authors identify WFDC3 as a key gene mediating prognostic regulation, linking specific cellular ecosystems to high-risk disease. The work provides candidate prognostic biomarkers and a framework for understanding the spatial organization of ICC.
